name: Empty Red Waterskin
summary: The Empty Red Waterskin is a leather vessel entrusted to fledgling shaman during their elemental trials. It is used to collect fresh, untainted water from a surprising source in the plagued town of Tarren Mill.

sections.title: A Vessel for Pure Water
sections.body: Given by the hermit Brine in the Barrens, this plain red skin serves a vital spiritual purpose in the Call of Water trials. Initiates are tasked with carrying it far across the sea to the Hillsbrad Foothills, seeking out the town of Tarren Mill. Though the town is occupied by the Forsaken and steeped in undeath, a lone well in its center continues to draw sweet, pristine spring water. Filling the red waterskin captures a vital sample of life persevering amidst blight, which Brine blends into a vial of purest water for the initiate's trial.

faq.q: What is the Empty Red Waterskin used for?
aliases: what to do with red waterskin
faq.answer: It is used by shaman on the Call of Water questline to collect spring water from the well in Tarren Mill, transforming it into a Filled Red Waterskin.
Brine, an orc shaman hermit living on a hill in the southern Barrens, gives it to shaman initiates undergoing the elemental trials.

faq.q: Why gather water from Tarren Mill specifically?
faq.answer: Despite Tarren Mill falling under the control of the Forsaken, the central well remains completely uncorrupted. Brine sees this pure spring as a powerful elemental symbol of hope and enduring life surviving in an unhallowed land.

faq.q: What happens after the waterskin is filled?
faq.answer: Once filled at the well, the skin must be brought back to Brine in the Barrens, who combines the water with other rare samples into a vial of purest water, from which Islen Waterseer creates the Water Sapta.

angles.text: Carrying and filling this waterskin is a foundational step in mastering the Water Totem and attuning your senses to the resilient spirits of water.
Brine compares the pure well in Tarren Mill to Warchief Thrall—a beacon of unyielding strength and hope enduring through immense suffering.
